findings.description: Policy-resource ownership is inconsistent with installation and inventory comparison.
findings.analysis: The scanner checksums every regular file below policies, while init currently copies only top-level Markdown policy files. Nested or non-Markdown package policy resources would therefore be reported as drift after init; a non-Markdown target policy file would also be treated as managed.
findings.recommendation: Keep policies as top-level Markdown documents and make scanning and installation use that same rule. Mark package-owned policy documents in standard YAML frontmatter so stale owned policies can be removed without touching user-added files.
findings.rationale: Policies remain intentionally simple: top-level Markdown only. User-added policy files must never be removed, so package ownership must be explicit rather than inferred from a filename or location.

findings.description: Blueprint validation does not currently reject a package without the required specle skill or policy documents.
findings.analysis: Init rejects a package without the specle skill or any policy documents, whereas blueprint validation currently checks only the managed scan, lifecycle, and generated index model. CI could therefore accept a package that init cannot deploy.
findings.recommendation: Move package-completeness validation into the shared inventory operation so init and blueprint validation consume the same result.
findings.rationale: A common inventory operation must own the complete package contract, not merely traversal. Init and blueprint validation must not carry divergent completeness rules.

findings.description: Blueprint scan failures can escape validate as an uncaught traceback.
findings.analysis: Installed-target validation converts a SkillMetadataError into a diagnostic, but the blueprint branch calls the same scanner without that boundary. Invalid packaged metadata would therefore produce a traceback instead of normal validation output.
findings.recommendation: Accept. Make both validate modes convert inspection errors into concise diagnostics.
findings.rationale: The shared inventory operation can fail for either root. CLI validation must expose those failures consistently as diagnostics rather than a traceback.

findings.description: The retained policy-discovery compatibility helper now requires a sibling managed skill inventory.
findings.analysis: discover_policies() delegates to the distribution scan. A caller that supplies only a policies directory now fails before discovering its Markdown documents. No current production caller needs standalone policy discovery.
findings.recommendation: Remove the obsolete discover_policies compatibility helper and its test-only callers. Do not restore an independent policy traversal.
findings.rationale: The helper has no production caller and is not a supported public compatibility contract. Retaining it creates dead code and invites a second discovery path.

findings.description: Managed-resource checksums load each whole resource into memory.
findings.analysis: The implementation uses read_bytes before SHA-256. Current skills and resources are tiny; the review extrapolates to arbitrarily large package resources without an established need.
findings.recommendation: Decline for this bounded skills distribution unless resource types or sizes expand.
findings.rationale: Current package resources are small and bounded. Streaming hashes add complexity without a present requirement; reconsider only if supported resource types or sizes expand.

findings.description: Validation can observe a transient mixed state during concurrent installation.
findings.analysis: This assumes an independently running validate command precisely while init replaces managed paths. The project does not establish concurrent installation or validation as a supported workflow.
findings.rationale: Specle does not support concurrent installation and validation against one target. Do not add locking or generation-snapshot machinery for this hypothetical race.

findings.description: An installed target with no managed skills reports an empty inventory instead of every expected missing skill.
findings.analysis: The scanner currently raises before the installed and blueprint inventories can be compared. The result is still a validation failure, but it is less specific than the promised per-skill drift diagnostics.
findings.recommendation: Accept if actionable drift diagnostics are a requirement for wholly missing or marker-stripped managed inventory; otherwise retain the simpler structural failure.
findings.rationale: Installed validation should compare an empty managed inventory with the blueprint inventory and report the missing managed skills individually. Blueprint inspection remains non-empty by contract.

findings.description: The matching-record test compares names and resources but not the complete parsed metadata objects.
findings.analysis: Any metadata change in SKILL.md also changes its checksum, so production drift detection already catches it. The requested assertion would make the test more direct but does not add a distinct production behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Decline unless the test is being tightened as part of another accepted production correction.
findings.rationale: Checksums already detect all SKILL.md frontmatter changes, and generated-index validation detects description or usage changes. The additional assertion duplicates production coverage without adding behaviour.

findings.description: Drift tests assert the diagnostic class but not the exact affected resource path.
findings.analysis: The tests prove the changed target produces a drift failure but do not prove the diagnostic names that target. This is a test-specific precision improvement.
findings.recommendation: Decline unless an accepted production diagnostic change needs direct coverage.
findings.rationale: No accepted production diagnostic change requires this extra assertion. Do not add test-only precision work without a distinct behaviour requirement.

findings.description: The binary-resource test does not prove the binary resource is detected when drifted.
findings.analysis: The scanner includes the binary file because it uses byte reads, but the test only asserts a clean initial comparison. This is test-strengthening rather than a known production defect.
findings.recommendation: Decline. Binary resources are not an intended supported Specle distribution class.
findings.rationale: Specle does not intend to distribute binary resources. Do not expand tests or preserve behaviour around an unsupported resource type.

findings.description: Package-completeness diagnostics remain outside the shared inventory result.
findings.analysis: scan_managed_inventory() returns skills, policy resources, and lifecycle analysis, but callers must separately invoke validate_package_inventory(). This leaves package completeness outside the single inventory contract and creates another rule that init and blueprint validation must remember to apply, contrary to the accepted requirement that the inventory result centralise package-completeness analysis.
findings.recommendation: Move package-completeness diagnostics into the shared inventory result and have init and blueprint validation consume that result directly.
findings.rationale: The inventory scan is the authoritative reusable contract. Package-completeness diagnostics belong in its result so all consumers use the same analysis without remembering an extra validation call.

findings.description: Forced initialisation can overwrite an unmarked user policy that shares a package filename.
findings.analysis: The ownership marker limits obsolete-policy deletion, but the staged replacement path still replaces every incoming package policy destination when `--force` is supplied. An existing unmarked `.agents/policies/testing.md`, for example, is backed up and overwritten by the packaged `testing.md`. This defeats the explicit ownership boundary for a same-name user document and is destructive despite the document being unmarked.
findings.recommendation: Treat an unmarked existing policy at an incoming package path as a collision even with `--force`; report it for user resolution rather than overwriting it.
findings.rationale: The normal preflight already reports occupied managed destinations and aborts without `--force`. Supplying `--force` explicitly authorises replacement at those paths, including user policies and skills.
